heading: Describe your whole family
intro: Describe the people traveling before choosing the program. Share ages, interests, preferred language and the room, food or mobility arrangements you need the provider to confirm. Ask for specific answers rather than assuming the family label addresses every requirement. You do not need a detailed activity list yet; first establish whether the proposed services match the group you are planning for.
points: Share ages and ask about provider-specific participation requirements for each proposed activity.
State any mobility limitations to arrange appropriate boat seating or walking breaks.
Specify dietary needs like allergies or preferences for local versus familiar foods.

heading: Choose a realistic rhythm
intro: Build the day around a pace your family can discuss together. Compare activity time with transfers, meals and rest rather than judging the number of outings. Ask about walking effort, early starts and shared-group arrangements for the actual program. If different travelers want different rhythms, confirm the choices and any extra services needed before relying on a flexible description.
points: Indicate maximum hours per day for active excursions versus relaxing downtime.
Confirm preference for early morning departures or later starts based on energy levels.
Describe the balance you want between offered activities and rest at the accommodation.

heading: Ask about each activity
intro: Ask about each proposed outing rather than applying one answer to the whole trip. The provider should explain participation requirements, the route, equipment and accompanying adults. Compare those details with your group’s needs and interests. Keep invited host visits separate from assumptions about access, and do not treat an attractive activity name as confirmation that everyone in the family can join.
points: Select preferred activities and note any equipment requirements such as waterproof boots.
Confirm interest in cultural interactions while respecting community privacy and invitation rules.
Identify physical demands to ensure the itinerary matches current fitness levels.

heading: Confirm rooms and meals
intro: Compare the actual rooms and meals with the arrangements your family needs. Ask for the bed layout, bathrooms and any requirements for staying together, then describe food needs clearly. Confirm what the provider can supply and include for the chosen dates. Photos and broad room categories can help frame questions, but they do not establish that specific facilities or meal arrangements are available.
points: State room type preferences including bed configurations and bathroom facilities needed.
Request specific meal plans considering allergies, religious observances, or taste habits.
Ask about availability of private dining areas for family celebrations or quiet dinners.

heading: Include the complete journey
intro: Place every transfer in the family itinerary, including any journey outside the package. Ask how arrival, meals and rest fit together and what support is available for luggage or boarding. Compare the complete route with your onward plans. The regional base alone cannot tell you how the actual travel day will work for your group or which services need separate booking.
points: Confirm whether airport or city transfers are included in the proposed booking.
Ask about luggage limits and assistance needs during road or river transitions.
Verify availability of quiet hours to recharge after active days on the water.

heading: Agree on alternatives and terms
intro: Discuss alternatives and the complete family price before paying. Ask what happens if an outing changes or someone skips an activity, and who accompanies each traveler in that situation. Compare the quote using the actual ages, group, rooms and dates. Mark exclusions and additional services, and keep the change terms alongside the agreed itinerary so the proposal is easy to review.
points: Inquire about alternative dates or locations if primary choices are unavailable.
Review cancellation terms and understand deposit rules for non-refundable bookings.
Ask for the complete price, exclusions and separately charged activities for your actual family group.
